mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks indicates an underlying momentum of recovery, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: As people spend less time at home, indicated by the sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, they are increasingly engaging in out-of-home activities, directly boosting retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases above 16% in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent recovery in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility suggests a broader return to daily routines, including commuting, which will lead to increased incidental retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES or TRANSIT mobility declines significantly (more than 2 percentage points week-on-week) in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: The observed broad-based recovery across all mobility categories, especially the strong rebound in PARKS, indicates an easing of local restrictions or a shift in public sentiment towards greater outdoor activity, which will spill over into RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, reflecting essential outings, suggests a growing comfort with out-of-home activities, which will translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as discretionary spending increases.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility decreases for two consecutive weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility from t-1w to t-0w (from -51.4 to -37.3) indicates a strong surge in outdoor activity, which will precede and drive an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next one week as people extend their outings.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility increases by more than 10 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next week despite PARKS mobility increasing by more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of decreasing RESIDENTIAL time and increasing WORKPLACES activity signifies a shift away from home-bound lifestyles, creating more opportunities for retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases while WORKPLACES mobility decreases over the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent upward trend in TRANSIT mobility, even at low levels, suggests a gradual increase in public transport usage, which is a leading indicator for increased foot traffic in retail and recreation areas over the next four weeks, especially in an urban setting like Milan.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility declines for two consecutive weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks.
